activateRegistrationTokenDeposit(uint256.details: Deposit a token security deposit for the service registration after its activation.

returns.isTokenSecured: True if the service Id is token secured, false if ETH secured otherwise.

createWithToken(uint256,address,uint32[].details: Creates a record with the token-related information for the specified service.

drain(address).details: Drains slashed funds to the drainer address.

getAgentBond(uint256,uint256).details: Gets the agent Id bond in a specified service.

returns.bond: Agent Id bond in a specified service Id.

getOperatorBalance(address,uint256).details: Gets the operator's balance in a specified service.

returns._0: True if the service Id is token secured.

registerAgentsTokenDeposit(address,uint2.details: Deposits bonded tokens from the operator during the agent instance registration.

params.agentIds: Set of agent Ids for corresponding agent instances opertor is registering.

returns.isTokenSecured: True if the service Id is token secured, false if ETH secured otherwise.

resetServiceToken(uint256).details: Resets a record with token and security deposit data.

terminateTokenRefund(uint256).details: Refunds a token security deposit to the service owner after the service termination.

returns.securityRefund: Returned token security deposit, or zero if the service is ETH-secured.

unbondTokenRefund(address,uint256).details: Refunds bonded tokens to the operator during the unbond phase.

returns.refund: Returned bonded token amount, or zero if the service is ETH-secured.

createWithToken(uint256,address,uint32[].notice: We assume that the token is checked for being a non-zero address and a non-ETH address representation         outside of this function. Here we optimistically check for the token to have a specific `balanceOf()`         view function. It is possible this is the attacker token that has all the required functions defined         correctly, so there is no point in checking that formality. All the required checks will be done in-place         where the possibility of misbehavior can be caught by return values of token function.

registerAgentsTokenDeposit(address,uint2.notice: This is an optimistic implementation corresponding to registering agent instances by the operator         assuming that this function is always called in pair with the original Service Registry agent instance         registration function, where all the necessary validity checks are provided.
